$comment: Components that ship inside PokitPlayer installers but are NOT visible to npm. npm only sees the wrapper packages; it cannot see the binaries they fetch or vendor.

As of the LGPL migration (2026-09-03) the ffmpeg-static and ffprobe-static npm packages are GONE. Binaries now come from scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.js (Windows/Linux, pinned URL + SHA-256) or scripts/build-ffmpeg-macos.sh (macOS, compiled from pinned source).

EVIDENCE: every 'configuration' string below was read directly out of the shipped binary - FFmpeg compiles its configure line into the executable. Re-verify at any time with `npm run ffmpeg:verify`, which fails the build on any GPL or non-distributable flag.
Do not edit license fields from memory.

components.name: Electron
notes: The application runtime.

Electron itself is MIT, but the shipped runtime embeds Chromium and Node.js, whose own component notices are enumerated in LICENSES.chromium.html (9.2 MB) inside the Electron distribution. electron-builder copies that file into the packaged app.
Electron 28 is end-of-life; see PINNED.md.

components.name: Chromium
notes: Embedded in Electron 28.3.3, not consumed independently.
Its own third-party components are enumerated in LICENSES.chromium.html, shipped verbatim in the Electron distribution.
That file is the authoritative notice for this component - hand it to counsel as-is rather than re-summarising it.

components.name: Node.js
notes: Embedded in Electron 28.3.3.

components.name: FFmpeg (Electron internal libffmpeg)
components.configuration: libavformat license: LGPL version 2.1 or later
notes: DISTINCT from the standalone ffmpeg CLI below, and licensed separately.
This is Chromium's internal media library (libffmpeg.so / .dylib / .dll), dynamically linked into the Electron runtime and used by the <video> element.
Verified LGPL, NOT GPL: the string 'libavformat license: LGPL version 2.1 or later' is compiled into the shipped library.
LGPL dynamic linking is satisfied here - the library is a separate shared object the user could replace.
Electron's default build enables proprietary codecs (H.264 / AAC); that raises a PATENT question, not an open-source licence question. See the audit memo.

components.name: FFmpeg CLI tools (ffmpeg + ffprobe)
components.configuration: --prefix=/ffbuild/prefix --pkg-config-flags=--static --pkg-config=pkg-config --cross-prefix=x86_64-w64-mingw32- --arch=x86_64 --target-os=mingw32 --enable-version3 --disable-debug --disable-w32threads --enable-pthreads --enable-iconv --enable-zlib --enable-libxml2 --enable-libvmaf --enable-fontconfig --enable-libharfbuzz --enable-libfreetype --enable-libfribidi --enable-vulkan --enable-libvorbis --enable-gmp --enable-lzma --enable-opencl --enable-amf --enable-libaom --enable-libdav1d --enable-ffnvcodec --enable-cuda-llvm --disable-frei0r --enable-libkvazaar --enable-libass --enable-libmp3lame --enable-libopus --enable-libtheora --enable-libvpx --enable-libwebp --enable-libvpl --enable-libopenh264 --enable-libopenjpeg --disable-librubberband --enable-libsnappy --enable-libsoxr --enable-libsvtav1 --enable-vaapi --disable-libvidstab --disable-libx264 --disable-libx265 --disable-libxavs2 --disable-libxvid --enable-libzimg --enable-libzvbi (full line in the binary; truncated here to the licence-relevant flags)
notes: Replaces the GPL-3 gyan.dev build the ffmpeg-static package used to download. One archive supplies both ffmpeg and ffprobe, so the ffprobe-vs-ffmpeg version mismatch recorded in PINNED.md is gone as a side effect.
Invoked only as a separate child process (child_process.spawn / execFile); there is no linking of any kind against the application code, and LGPL is satisfied by that boundary alone.

CAVEAT worth knowing: BtbN publishes LGPL variants only as master-branch snapshots under a rolling 'latest' tag, not as release-branch builds. We pin the exact SHA-256 so the artefact cannot change under us, and the licence gate re-checks every fetch. Building all three platforms from a pinned FFmpeg release tarball - as macOS already does - would remove both the master-snapshot and the third-party-trust question. See the audit memo.

components.name: FFmpeg CLI tools (ffmpeg + ffprobe)
components.supplier: Maiden Media Solutions INC. — compiled in CI by scripts/build-ffmpeg-macos.sh
licenceRelevantFlags: NO --enable-gpl (GPL is off by default in FFmpeg; we never turn it on)
NO --enable-version3, so this is the more permissive LGPL-2.1-or-later
No external libraries at all — encoding uses VideoToolbox, an Apple OS framework
notes: macOS is the one platform with no published LGPL build from any reputable source: Homebrew, evermeet.cx and osxexperts all ship --enable-gpl, and the arm64 binary the old ffmpeg-static package downloaded was additionally --enable-nonfree and therefore not redistributable at all. Compiling is the only lawful option, so we compile.

Built natively on a runner of the target architecture - macos-14 for arm64, macos-13 for x64. Never cross-built and never shared between architectures; doing that is what previously put an arm64 binary inside the Intel DMG, where it could not execute.
--disable-autodetect is deliberate: it stops the build silently picking up whatever GPL libraries happen to be present on the build machine.
Slightly more permissive than the Windows/Linux builds (LGPL-2.1 vs LGPL-3) because nothing in it requires version3. Accurate rather than uniform.

components.name: OpenH264
components.version: bundled inside the FFmpeg CLI build
notes: The software H.264 encoder that replaced x264 in the playback pipeline. BSD-2-Clause, so it carries no copyleft obligation.

PATENT NOTE, kept separate from the licence question: Cisco's well-known H.264 royalty offer covers Cisco's OWN precompiled binary. Using a libopenh264 compiled by someone else does not automatically inherit that coverage. H.264 patent licensing is already a live consideration for this product because the player decodes H.264 regardless - see the audit memo.
Not used on macOS, where VideoToolbox handles encoding.

components.name: libvpx
components.version: bundled inside the FFmpeg CLI build
notes: VP9 encoder, used only as the last-resort fallback when no H.264 encoder is usable on the machine. BSD-3-Clause, no copyleft obligation.
When it is selected the renderer declares vp09.00.41.08 to MSE instead of avc1.640029; src/encoder.js keeps the encoder and the codec string paired so they cannot drift.
